## Trait Measurements Fountain-Jones et al.

## Results There were 45 (24 herbivorous, 12 predatory, six nectarivorous, and three detritivorous) species of beetles with six or more individuals for trait measurement (954 individuals in total of which 270 individuals were measured).
There were 21 (11 groundnesting, eight opportunistic, and two arboreal-nesting) species of ants that had six or more individuals for trait measurement (2268 individuals of which 126 were measured).
Summary of traits measured for beetles and ants and their possible functional links.
From this suite, we selected four key traits for beetles: body size, dispersal power (calculated as leg length divided by body length), color variation, and feeding guild (Table S1).
Feeding guild was excluded for ants since 20 of 21 species sampled were predators (with some opportunistic sap feeders), with only one herbivorous species found (Table S2).

rows.2: Each of its 21 species takes one row.

basisOfRecord.quote: Insects were sampled using a combination of pan traps, pitfall traps, and a vacuum sampler, with sampling conducted over three seasons.

Pitfall traps captured epigaeic insects using 70 mm diameter, 90 mm deep plastic containers, sufficiently wide to capture most invertebrates while minimizing vertebrate bycatch, inserted flush with the soil.
During sampling, lids were removed, and traps were halffilled with a 50% ethylene glycol solution and left open for 1 week before contents were processed and preserved in 75% ethanol.
Pan traps sampled aerial insects on calm, sunny days for maximum efficiency.

measurementStatistic.quote: For each species, six individuals were measured and averaged (see Table 1).
